facts.fact: The Ministry of Gender, Youth and Social Development's World Bank-financed PSLP seeks a consultant to build a real-time and bulk API authenticating national ID numbers against the National Identity and Civil Registry.

systems.owner: Ministry of Gender, Youth and Social Development

LSO.note: The document links NISSA to the national ID and civil registry, not births or deaths to the ID system.
Disability questions added to a data-collection form are not accessibility of information or services.
Digital payments mentioned only as a coming transition, no programme named.
No count or share of people holding a national ID.
Nothing on a number at birth.
Nothing on who runs or owns the ID system.

facts.fact: The ministry plans NISSA, the social registry, to authenticate national ID numbers before storing them, and says it is working with the National Identity and Civil Registry on an interoperability link.

systems.owner: Ministry of Gender, Youth and Social Development

LSO.note: The national ID system is named only as the authentication counterpart; nothing on its issuance, biometrics or certification.
Nothing on local government offices' connection.
Nothing on civil registration offices entering events digitally.

facts.fact: The ministry says it is working with the National Identity and Civil Registry (Ministry of Home Affairs) to establish an interoperability link with NISSA/MISSA, and a consultancy is sought to develop and test the API between them.

systems.owner: Ministry of Gender, Youth and Social Development

LSO.note: NISSA is a social registry, not a programme management information system; no programme system, payments or several-programme use is stated.

facts.fact: The ministry says NISSA, the national social registry run by the Director of Social Assistance, currently holds 90% (488,000) of Basotho households across all 10 districts, and is being updated through the World Bank-financed PSLP.
